reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is the 2D-to-3D lifting ambiguity: a single planar projection admits infinitely many 3D rays. Backprojection reduces this to a 4D manifold (two intersection points with ground and vertical planes), eliminating camera location and orientation. The bidirectional LSTM then processes temporal differences ΔP_t, which are shift-invariant and capture local dynamics. Crucially, height h is a scalar invariant under horizontal rotation, allowing separate prediction. The end-of-trajectory (EoT) classifier provides a soft segmentation criterion, preventing over-extrapolation. Together, these components form a minimal sufficient statistic for 3D ball kinematics under the assumed physics.
